page: Microsoft Azure DS13_v2 is a DSv2-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. The CPU configuration provides 1.0 thread per core, supported by a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 35 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 56.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.0 GB of RAM per core. It includes 115 GB of local storage and does not feature any GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data shows a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core metrics, including stress-ng single-core CPU performance, gzip compression, and Geekbench single-core scores, consistently fall into the weak category, representing the bottom 25% of tested hardware. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels within the middle 50% across stress-ng multi-core, bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core tests. Memory bandwidth remains average, with read-only cached small block speeds at 720.03 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 76.69 GB/sec.

This hardware profile is suited for workloads that benefit from a high memory-to-vCPU ratio but do not require high single-threaded compute performance. Database operations, static web serving, and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, making the server viable for relational databases, caching layers, and general-purpose backend applications. However, the weak single-core performance and weak medium-model LLM inference speeds, such as 7.18 tokens/sec for a 7B model, represent significant tradeoffs for compute-heavy or modern AI workloads.
